topic: PMI Certified Professional in Managing AI (PMI-CPMAI) exam preparation - PMI's certification for managing AI initiatives end to end using the CPMAI Methodology (originally from Cognilytica, acquired by PMI in 2024): responsible AI, business and data understanding, data preparation, model development and evaluation, and operationalization, with the go/no-go gate discipline that distinguishes AI projects from traditional software projects
cert_name: PMI Certified Professional in Managing AI
exam_format: 120 multiple-choice/multiple-select questions (100 scored + 20 unscored pretest), 160 minutes, computer-based at Pearson VUE test centers or online proctored (OnVue). Offered in English plus Arabic, Brazilian Portuguese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Simplified & Traditional Chinese, and Spanish since January 2026. PMI does not publish a fixed passing score. IMPORTANT eligibility rule: completion of PMI's own PMI-CPMAI Exam Prep Course is REQUIRED before scheduling the exam - there are no experience prerequisites. Up to three attempts within a 1-year eligibility period; retakes require an additional fee. Certification is maintained with 30 PDUs every 3 years under PMI's CCR program. Pricing (~$699 exam bundle, retake ~$300) varies by region and PMI membership - present all fees as approximate and advise verifying current PMI pricing.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'; predominantly scenario-based questions asking what the AI project manager should do FIRST/NEXT/BEST within a specific CPMAI phase
audience: Project managers, program managers, and PMP holders adding AI delivery skills; product managers and business analysts leading AI initiatives; data/AI team leads who need lifecycle and governance discipline; and professionals targeting AI transformation roles. No prior AI, technical, or project management experience is formally required, making it accessible to ambitious beginners while remaining highly relevant to experienced PMs.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Support Responsible and Trustworthy AI Efforts
domains.notes: PMI's official Domain I. Privacy and security plans: data governance for PII, encryption and access controls for training data, privacy impact assessments, GDPR/CCPA compliance, secure data handling across the AI lifecycle. AI/ML transparency: documenting model and data selection rationale, explainability requirements, audit trails for algorithmic decisions, interpretability tools. Bias checks across model, data, and algorithm: representation analysis, fairness testing across population groups, bias detection metrics, mitigation techniques. Monitoring evolving AI regulation and sector-specific compliance, coordinating with legal teams, and maintaining accountability documentation: version control for models/data/training, documented go/no-go decision points, chain of custody for data, and accountability reporting for executives and regulators.

domains.name: Identify Business Needs and Solutions
domains.notes: PMI's official Domain II and joint-largest domain. Identifying the problem to be solved: stakeholder interviews, process analysis for automation opportunities, personas and use cases, mapping business problems to AI patterns (anchor to the Seven Patterns of AI), validating with SMEs. Evaluating initial AI feasibility - technical viability, data availability, compute constraints, organizational readiness, and honestly comparing AI against traditional alternatives. Risk assessments across security, safety, and ethics. Drafting the AI project scope statement with success criteria and in/out-of-scope boundaries. Determining ROI and total cost of ownership, building the business case, managing adoption and integration risks (change management, user resistance, training), drafting the high-level AI solution architecture, defining KPIs and success thresholds, and identifying resources: team skills, hardware/infrastructure, and contractor gaps.

domains.name: Identify Data Needs
domains.notes: PMI's official Domain III and joint-largest domain - reflecting the CPMAI axiom that AI projects are data projects. Defining required data: types, formats, volume, sampling, temporal and granularity requirements, quality standards. Identifying data SMEs, data stewards, and governance teams. Mapping data sources: internal warehouses, external/third-party providers, cloud repositories, legacy archives, plus ownership and access permissions. Coordinating the AI workspace and infrastructure: compute provisioning, secure dev environments, storage, collaboration and version control tooling. Gathering data: extraction, transfers, ongoing feeds, completeness validation, refresh procedures. Checking privacy, licensing, compliance, and access; overseeing data evaluation (quality dimensions, distributions, bias and gap analysis, exploratory data analysis); making the data go/no-go decision on whether data meets solution needs; and conveying data understanding to leadership in business language.

domains.name: Manage AI Model Development and Evaluation
domains.notes: PMI's official Domain IV. Overseeing model technique selection: matching algorithms to use cases, supervised vs unsupervised vs reinforcement approaches, complexity-performance-interpretability trade-offs, coordinating with data scientists on architecture. Model QA/QC: testing protocols, configuration management for versions and parameters, performance monitoring during development, peer reviews. Managing training: schedules, compute utilization, hyperparameter tuning, cross-validation, experiment tracking and data versioning. Managing data transformation and preparation: cleaning, feature engineering, normalization, augmentation and synthetic data, reproducibility. Two explicit gate decisions the exam loves: verifying data quality for the go/no-go into data preparation, and verifying the model is ready for the operationalization go/no-go - performance against success criteria, robustness and generalization, deployment readiness, and documented approval.

domains.name: Operationalize AI Solution
domains.notes: PMI's official Domain V. Deployment planning: strategy, timeline, infrastructure, IT coordination, rollback and contingency procedures, deployment checklists. Managing the deployment itself: cross-team coordination, issue resolution, production validation, access provisioning, post-deployment verification. Model governance in production: lifecycle management, versioning and change control, drift detection and monitoring, retraining schedules, policy compliance. Overseeing solution metrics: dashboards for business KPIs and model performance, degradation analysis, stakeholder reporting, threshold alerting. Closing the loop: final report and lessons learned, knowledge transfer documentation, the transition plan from project team to operational support with defined roles, and the contingency plan - incident response for AI failures, backup/disaster recovery, escalation, business continuity, and regular testing of those procedures.

extra_guidance: PMI-CPMAI is PMI's flagship AI certification (built on Cognilytica's CPMAI Methodology after PMI's September 2024 acquisition) and one of the fastest-growing credentials in project management in 2026 - the PMI brand brings an enormous PMP-holder audience, and this course cross-sells naturally with the catalog's AIPMM CPM/CDPM product-management courses. Use PMI's OFFICIAL September 2025 Exam Content Outline as gospel: the five domain names and weights in this config are PMI's official figures (15/26/26/16/17) - use them verbatim and cover every task listed in the domain notes; the notes mirror the official tasks and enablers. Anchor everything to the CPMAI Methodology's six phases - Business Understanding, Data Understanding, Data Preparation, Model Development, Model Evaluation, Operationalization - and its core doctrines: AI projects are DATA projects first (which is why the two 26% domains are business and data), iterate in short phases rather than waterfall, and enforce explicit go/no-go gates between phases (the exam repeatedly tests recognizing WHICH phase a scenario is in and whether to proceed). Weave in the Seven Patterns of AI (hyperpersonalization, autonomous systems, predictive analytics/decision support, conversation/human interaction, patterns and anomalies, recognition, goal-driven systems) when mapping business problems to AI approaches, and PMI's responsible-AI framing throughout. CRITICAL honesty notes: (a) completion of PMI's own PMI-CPMAI Exam Prep Course is REQUIRED to schedule the exam - state this clearly and position this course as exam-focused reinforcement and practice alongside PMI's official course, never as a replacement or a path around the requirement; (b) PMI does not publish a passing score - do not invent one; (c) present all fees as approximate with regional/membership variation. Practice questions MUST be predominantly scenario-based with 'FIRST / NEXT / BEST / MOST appropriate' framing - e.g. a model performing well on training data but failing fairness testing (which gate, what action), a sponsor pushing to skip data understanding, drift detected post-deployment - plus phase-identification and multiple-select questions clearly marked 'Select TWO/THREE' to mirror the real format. Keep the course vendor-agnostic like the exam: name cloud/ML tools only as interchangeable examples, and scan the practice bank so no question depends on AWS/Azure/GCP-specific knowledge. Frame everything as 'exam-focused preparation' - never promise a pass, guarantee, or first-attempt success (Udemy compliance; never emit the word 'guarantee' in any form). Final chapter must be a full 120-question exam simulation strategy walkthrough with 160-minute time management (about 80 seconds per question, flag-and-return, no scheduled breaks), Pearson VUE test-day logistics for both test-center and OnVue online-proctored delivery, and the three-attempts-in-one-year retake policy.
